learningObjectives.title: Places of worship and their features

questions.q: What best describes liturgical worship?
options: Worship that follows a set, structured order or pattern
Worship carried out only in private at home
Spontaneous worship with no fixed structure
Worship that never uses the Bible
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a fixed liturgy, an agreed order of service used regularly.

questions.q: What is a key feature of non-liturgical worship?
options: It does not follow a fixed, set order of service
It must always be led by a bishop
It always uses incense and set prayers
It can only take place in a cathedral
questions.explain: Non-liturgical worship is less formal and does not follow a set, unchanging structure.

questions.q: Which of these is the clearest example of liturgical worship?
options: A spontaneous prayer group in someone's home
questions.explain: The Mass follows a set liturgy, making it a classic example of liturgical worship.

questions.q: A church service has no set order, includes spontaneous prayer, lively music and personal testimony. This is best classed as:
questions.explain: The lack of a fixed structure and spontaneous elements make it non-liturgical worship.

questions.q: How do Quakers characteristically worship?
options: In mostly silent meetings without a set liturgy or minister
By following a fixed Latin Mass
questions.explain: Quaker worship is based on silent waiting on God, with no set liturgy or ordained minister.

questions.q: Why do many Christians value liturgical worship?
options: Its familiar shared structure unites the congregation across time and place
It allows worshippers to avoid using any prayers
It removes the need for a place of worship
It guarantees worship is never repeated
questions.explain: A shared, familiar order gives a sense of unity and continuity with Christians everywhere.

questions.q: Which prayer did Jesus teach his followers?
questions.explain: The Lord's Prayer (the 'Our Father') was taught by Jesus as a model for prayer.

questions.q: A worshipper prays to say sorry to God for wrongdoing. This type of prayer is best described as:
questions.explain: Confession (penitence) is prayer expressing sorrow and asking forgiveness for sin.

questions.q: How many sacraments are recognised by the Roman Catholic Church?
questions.explain: Catholicism recognises seven sacraments, including baptism, Eucharist and marriage.

questions.q: Most Protestant Churches recognise only two sacraments. Which two are they?
options: Anointing of the sick and holy orders
questions.explain: Many Protestants keep only baptism and the Eucharist as sacraments commanded by Jesus.

questions.q: At a service, bread and wine are shared to remember Jesus' Last Supper. This sacrament is the:
questions.explain: Sharing bread and wine in memory of the Last Supper is the Eucharist (Holy Communion).

questions.q: The Eucharist is also commonly known by which other name?
questions.explain: The Eucharist is also called Holy Communion, the Lord's Supper or the Mass.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the sacrament of baptism?
options: To welcome a person into the Christian community and cleanse from sin
To ordain a person as a priest
To bless a new church building
questions.explain: Baptism marks initiation into the Church and symbolises washing away sin.

questions.q: What is 'intercession' in Christian prayer?
options: Praying on behalf of the needs of other people
questions.explain: Intercession means asking God to help others, praying for their needs.

questions.q: In a church, what is the font mainly used for?
questions.explain: The font holds the water used in the sacrament of baptism.

questions.q: A minister stands at a raised platform to deliver the sermon. This feature is the:
questions.explain: The pulpit is the raised stand used for preaching the sermon.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the altar in many churches?
options: It is the table where the Eucharist is celebrated
It is where the congregation is baptised
It is where the choir stores music
It is the entrance porch of the church
questions.explain: The altar is the table on which the bread and wine of the Eucharist are consecrated.

questions.q: In an Orthodox church, what is the iconostasis?
options: A screen decorated with icons separating the sanctuary from the congregation
questions.explain: The iconostasis is a screen covered with icons dividing the sanctuary from the nave.

questions.q: A Quaker meeting house is typically very plain, with chairs arranged in a circle or square and no altar. Why?
options: Quaker worship focuses on silent, direct communion with God without ritual objects
Quakers reject the existence of God
Quakers require a bishop to lead every service
questions.explain: The plain layout reflects Quaker emphasis on simplicity and unmediated, silent worship.

questions.q: In many churches, what is the lectern used for?
options: Reading the Bible aloud to the congregation
questions.explain: The lectern is the stand from which the scripture readings are read to the congregation.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Christianity: Worship
